brief:
Build contract M (below) in chongdae.py only, on top of commit 0ae52cf: a minimal change to the narrow path projection (path_prefixes / public_projection) so a machine path wrapped in `**...**` at a path start is projected with both wrappers kept and the raw mirror exact. Nothing else: no general Markdown, HTML or ANSI handling, no change to neutral_path (narrow=False) or its callers, no public argv exception, no adjacent architecture work, no new CLI command, setting or record key, no README change, no version bump; do not commit. The tests that decide M are written and protected: test_public_projection.py (43 earlier tests plus 16 M tests), test_record_transactions.py, test_chongdae.py and test_concurrency.py — do not change any of them; if one contradicts M, say so in `disputed-tests`. Do not touch README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the three manifests, SELFHOSTING.md, hunsu.json or hunsu.lock.json (a check hashes them). Checks are targeted; one final full suite runs later on the release candidate, not in this task. The session runs this run with python/python3 pinned to 3.11 through a link under a temp dir (<tmp>).

Contract M: a machine path wrapped in Markdown strong emphasis (`**...**`) is projected. Narrow follow-up to contract R (final), on top of commit 0ae52cf. Found by the session's complete-byte export scan of run run-20261030-091750-7101: a worker summary held `- **<tmp> (outside HOME):** fails.` and the public projection left that temporary path raw, because `*` is not in R1's path-start set. Today (0ae52cf, home mocked as /home/person, project root /work/project) every example below stays unchanged.

M1 A wrapper opens a path. A `**` that itself sits at a path start — at the start of the string, or right after whitespace, a quote, a backtick, or one of = ( [ , : ; | & > (R1's set) — and is followed immediately by a machine prefix (the project root, the home, a temporary directory, by R1/R2's rules) makes that prefix begin a path: the prefix is projected and the opening `**` is kept exactly. Examples: `- **<tmp> (outside HOME):** fails.` -> `- **<tmp> (outside HOME):** fails.`; `**<tmp>` -> `**<tmp>**`; `see **<tmp> now` -> `see **<tmp>** now`; `**/home/person/notes**` -> `**~/notes**`; `**/home/person**` -> `**~**`; `**/work/project/src/a.py**` -> `**./src/a.py**`; `**/work/project**` -> `**.**`.

M2 The closing markup is kept. For a path opened by such a wrapper, a `**` right after the path closes it and is not part of the path: the temporary-directory rule's "whole path under it" stops before it, and the home and project-root right boundary accepts it, so the closing `**` stays byte-for-byte (as in every M1 example). Paths not opened by a wrapper keep today's behavior exactly.

M3 Guards. A `**` that is not at a path start opens nothing: `src**<tmp>`, `a**<tmp>`, `docs**/home/person/x` and `docs**/work/project/x` stay unchanged, as every relative path does (R1). Only `**` is recognized: a single `*`, `_`, `__`, HTML, ANSI escapes or any other markup are not parsed and keep today's behavior. No general Markdown, HTML or ANSI handling is added.

M4 The raw mirror stays exact. For every string M1 changes, merge_private(public, raws) from public_projection equals the original string; through save_state the public file holds the projected form, the ignored local overlay the exact raw, and load_state (also in a new process) returns the exact raw.

M5 Nothing else changes. neutral_path (narrow=False) and its callers keep their behavior exactly; every guarantee of contracts P, P2-rel and R (R1-R7, R3a) stays true, including R6's projection of public checks (no public argv exception) and R3's refusal of machine-path keys. Scope: chongdae.py only, a minimal change to the narrow path projection; no CLI command, setting or record key.

These test names do not contain the section id (F1/F2): the amendment names existing tests, and renaming them would change other tests' identity. So a check cannot select them by section id, only by name.

The F2 expectations are built with the engine's own helpers (portable_argv, neutral_path, public_projection), as the brief allows. So they check that the recorded command matches that projection of the given argv. They cannot catch a bug inside those helpers; test_public_projection.py covers that.
